content.rendered:
1973: Bruce and the E Street Band play a gig at Nassau Community College in Garden City, New York. The show is filmed, and snippets of it have been aired at special events and in documentaries.

1977: Bruce and the E Street Band work on “Adam Raised a Cain” at a recording session  at The Record Plant in New York City.

1978: Bruce and the band play their first of two nights at the Winterland Ballroom in San Francisco on the Darkness Tour, and it will go down in history as one of their best. Broadcast live on KSAN-FM and captured as a soundboard recording, this show will be prolifically bootlegged for decades to come. It will finally be officially released more than four decades later as part of Bruce’s archive series–get it here.

1980: Bruce and the boys play their first of two River Tour nights at the Boston Garden.

1995: Bruce plays his first of two solo acoustic shows at the Orpheum Theater in Boston, where he plays every song from The Ghost of Tom Joad for the last time to date.

2001: Bruce makes a guest appearance with Tim McLoone’s Holiday Express at the Continental Airlines Arena in East Rutherford.

2007: Bruce and the E Street Band bring the Magic Tour to the Odyssey Arena in Belfast.

2012: Bruce joins The Rolling Stones on stage at the Prudential Center in Newark, joining Mick Jagger on vocals for “Tumbling Dice.”

2017: Springsteen on Broadway continues its theatrical run at the Walter Kerr Theater in New York City.

2018: Springsteen on Broadway closes its theatrical run at the Walter Kerr Theater in New York City. In attendance tonight: Oprah Winfrey. Shortly after the show ends, Netflix releases the show on streaming video.

2020: Bruce appears on a television special entitled Play On: Celebrating the Power of Music to Make Change, speaking in support of WhyHunger.

excerpt.rendered: On this date: Winterland ’78. Need I say more? (Okay, how about a Rolling Stones guest appearance and the streaming video release of Springsteen on Broadway?)

jetpack-related-posts.title: December 16
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: It's the debut of "Brothers Under the Bridge," the release of "The Wrestler," and the last "Crush on You" for 28 years as Bruce's tours start to wind down for the year.

jetpack-related-posts.title: December 27
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Born to Run and Darkness Tours wind down, and "Lost in the Flood" makes its last appearance for a quarter-century.

jetpack-related-posts.title: December 9
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On this date: Bruce surprises with a call-in to E Street Radio and a guest appearance with Gaslight Anthem, plus an emotional show the day after John Lennon's death. Much more inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: November 28
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Santa comes out in '99, an intense Magic show in Milan, and a unique Ramrod/Living on the Edge of the World mash-up--all and more from this date.

jetpack-related-posts.title: November 29
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On this date: Bruce releases the video for "War," gets his first opening act in 20 years, and plays his last show of the 20th century. More highlights inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: November 21
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On this date: Bruce releases his eleventh studio album, The Ghost of Tom Joad. Plus: the Seeger Sessions Tour wraps up, the return of forgotten classic "Song for Orphans," and Bruce plays his first ever show in Sweden. More highlights inside.
